learningObjective: Diagnose torch.compile graph breaks and recompiles from the TORCH_LOGS='+dynamo,recompiles' output and identify remediation strategies.

canonicalClaims.claim: torch.compile splits a function into subgraphs at data-dependent Python control flow (graph breaks) and keeps a shape-guarded compilation cache; enabling mark_dynamic on an input dim replaces multiple shape-specialized recompiles with one shape-generic compile.
conditions: The function contains data-dependent Python conditions or varying input shapes.
nonImplications: Does not imply mark_dynamic always speeds up steady-state execution.
Does not imply all graph breaks are avoidable.

misconceptions.claim: Graph breaks and shape-guard recompiles are the same issue.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Graph breaks come from Python-level control flow; guard recompiles from shape/dtype changes.

misconceptions.claim: Eliminating a graph break has no effect on compile behavior.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Removing a break re-merges subgraphs, unlocks cross-branch fusion, and can reduce overall compile churn.

misconceptions.claim: torch.compile always recompiles when shapes change.
misconceptions.whyWrong: With mark_dynamic or dynamic=True, one compilation covers a shape range.

misconceptions.claim: cache_size_limit is unrelated to shape guards.
misconceptions.whyWrong: The cache stores shape-specialized entries; the limit governs how many can coexist before eviction.
